provenance.orgName: Rochester, Kent. Cathedral priory of St Andrew
provenance.p: As well as the identification of this in the medieval catalogue, the script is a Rochester type like that in BL, Royal 5 C. i and 6 C. iv and the binding is similar to another Rochester manuscript, Bodley 387, and like that has the words 'S Wigorniae' on one of the endleaves (s. xvi). A strip has been cut from the bottom of fol. 1, which is the usual position for a Rochester inscription.

provenance.orgName: Windsor, Berkshire. Royal collegiate chapel of St George
provenance.p: Medieval binding similar to that of Bodley 387. Usual chain mark.

history.provenance: Cambridge, Cambridgeshire, Pembroke College (Aula Valence S. Marie)This attribution was never formally considered in any of the published handlists for Medieval Libraries of Great Britain (i.e. 1941, 1964, 1987). Later, during MLGB3 (2010-2015), the attribution was effectively rejected via the following note: There is not any evidence or probability that this manuscript was once at Pembroke, Cambridge, as guessed by M. R. James. Compare the Summary Catalogue: It was no. 190 = 2118 in Pembroke College (Cambridge) library.

provenance.orgName: Canterbury, Kent, Benedictine cathedral priory of Holy Trinity or Christ Church
provenance.p: This attribution was rejected in the second edition of Medieval Libraries of Great Britain (1964), which did not change in the Supplement (1987). The corresponding Medieval Libraries of Great Britain index card paraphrases the the Summary Catalogue, which was deemed unsatisfactory for an attribution: considered by M. R. James to be probably from Christ Church.

provenance.orgName: Worcester, Worcestershire, Benedictine cathedral priory of St Mary the Virgin
provenance.p: This attribution was rejected in the second edition of Medieval Libraries of Great Britain (1964), which did not change in the Supplement (1987). The corresponding Medieval Libraries of Great Britain index card records the following information, which was deemed unsatisfactory for an attribution: Wignorie (fol. 209v); C. H. Turner treats the name as presumptive evidence that the book belongs to Worcester at some moment in the later Middle Ages (Early Worcester Manuscripts, p. lxvi).

history.provenance: Said to have been given to Bodley by the Dean and Canons of Windsor in 1612.

recordHist.source: Neil R. Ker, ed., Medieval Libraries of Great Britain: A List of Surviving Books, Royal Historical Society Guides and Handbooks, 3 (London, 1941; 2nd edn, 1964; supplement, ed. Andrew G. Watson, 1987; digital edn, ed. Richard Sharpe and James M. W. Willoughby, 2010–15).
